blocks.x: Evidence-grade compliance without theater: controls mapped once across frameworks, evidence generated continuously by the systems themselves, and audits that start from a portal instead of a document hunt — with vendor blind spots named, not assumed away.
Audit readiness is a systems property, not an annual project

Compliance burns teams when it is a documentation sport: frameworks multiply, evidence is gathered by hand, and every audit becomes a fire drill. The fix is engineering — one control register mapped to many frameworks, evidence generated continuously from the systems themselves, and audits that read from the register instead of interrogating humans.
Digital trust extends this outward: customer due-diligence packs, vendor assurance, and the trust page that shows — with evidence — what you actually operate.
Below: the failure modes that turn compliance into archaeology, the reference architecture of continuous evidence, and the console that keeps first-time pass rates above target.
Four failure modes that turn compliance into archaeology
Every one of these costs the same audit twice — the countermeasures generate evidence where the control runs, so the artifact never goes stale.

widgets.title: An audit as a system run — click stages for the evidence contract

stages.name: Scope
stages.detail: Audit scope rendered from the control map: frameworks, periods, sampled controls — the auditor receives the map as data, not as a PDF.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.detail: Each sampled control's evidence pipeline exports its artifacts with timestamps and lineage — screenshots are replaced by queries.

stages.name: Walkthrough
stages.detail: Control walkthroughs run against the live system: show the access review job, the deploy gate, the encryption attestation — the demo is the walkthrough.

stages.name: Findings
stages.detail: Findings route into the same backlog as security work with owners and deadlines — compliance findings are engineering work, not a separate universe.

stages.name: Attest
stages.detail: The attestation report assembles from operating data; next audit starts from the same console — the compliance state is continuous.

widgets.note: Five stages, no archaeology: an audit is what the system already knows, sampled and demonstrated.
